stage: bounded exploration on already exposed development data
question: Does a two-observation prefix-slope initialization improve the frozen section3 state-space comparison?
change: Initialize at the second available observation: level=y1, slope=(y1-y0)/d; no first-two re-assimilation. Thereafter identical transitions, Q, R and Joseph updates.
initial_covariance: [[R,R/d],[R/d,2R/d^2+q*d/3]], q=acceleration_sigma^2; measurement and initial-interval process uncertainty propagated, diffuse initial-slope limit
interpretation: A coherent initialization change includes its prior covariance; do not attribute a difference to the slope mean alone. Observation/process noise scales are unchanged.
warmup: one-history forecast reuses original model; first transition each beam remains outside primary score
primary: same8 forecasts and equal-weight mean of per-beam MAEs; all11 target predictions exported
comparators: reuse original state-space and load-secant forecasts from stored CSV; do not rerun earlier experiments
information: prefix only, next nominal load specified; no next width or human endpoint used for initialization or tuning
uncertainty: working Gaussian95% bands and last-prefix-observation +/-1px sensitivity at fixed noise; no noise grid or calibrated coverage claim
sanity: zero-process-noise batch regression equivalence, two-observation secant equivalence, unequal loads, positive covariance, translation, future exclusion and no double counting
scope: same three beam sequences, section3; masks, data, previous results and MD01 unchanged; no neural training/inference
resource_cap: one CPU2x2 comparison plus fixed perturbations, <1min; no sweep
stop: save results and figures, report mixed effects and next decision; do not alter fixed noise or replace previous result
